_authority: Owner, 2026-10-20 (L61, course-factory 2.52.0): 'implement the layout templates. All slides for all modules that will be made need to be in this style, it's a RULE. Configure the compiler so it does this style - of course the logo should be our official one, and the colours from the brandbook.' The design is the owner-reviewed library design/course-layout-templates/ (preview.html, 13 templates, 2026-10-20); this file is its production contract.
rule: Every slide the compiler builds is one of the templates below, named on the slide as data-template="<id>.v1" with a supported data-variant. The compiler chooses it from the approved script and the build sheet; a build sheet may ask for a template or variant by name, and an unknown or unsuitable one is a problem with the slide's id. No slide invents its own structure or overrides the shared layout CSS (gb_layouts.css).

look.stylesheet: course-module-ui/templates/gb_layouts.css - loaded after gb_compose.css; every rule is scoped to [data-template], so a deck built before 2.52.0 looks as it did
look.stage: one logical 1280 x 800 slide: sizes in vmin with reading floors, so 1 vmin = 8 px at 1280 x 800 and the slide scales evenly on a projector
look.logo: the official file assets/novikontas_logo.svg (plugin/resources/brand), exactly as provided, top right of every slide; on a dark or photo slide it sits on a white plate (brandbook: only on a high-contrast background, safe area kept)
look.colours: brandbook only: Navy #0A2463, Novikontas Blue #53A7DB, Pitch Black #011111, Steel Blue #415C8F, Light Grey #E7EBF0, Pure White #FFFFFF. The reference design's amber is replaced by Novikontas Blue everywhere; the semantic correct / wrong / hazard colours of drawings and tasks stay what they are (they carry meaning, not brand)
look.type: Raleway - Bold titles, Medium body, SemiBold labels (brandbook); never smaller than the reading floors of gb_shell.css

split._why: 2.116.0 (operator Aleksis Vejs, 2026-11-09): the figure gets the share it needs - 40 % of the slide up to the whole slide; the old 50-60 % text band is no constraint. Default 55 / 45. A build sheet may set "split": 0.2 ... 0.6 (the text share).

boxes._why: the picture's box on a slide with words beside a picture comes in four sizes. The compiler (compile/scripts/layout_fit.py) gives a picture the smallest box that shows it readably and holds the words beside it; when the words do not fit beside that box they go in parts, and when a picture needs more than any box beside words (or growing it would cost the words more than extra_parts more parts) the factory does not squeeze it - the picture goes on the slide alone (figure-stage) or is made another kind of picture. A build sheet may name a box ("box": "picture-wide").
boxes._words: even is the measured beside_picture budget; the others in proportion to their column - starting values, the audits and the fit gate measure every build
boxes._extra_parts: growing the picture is worth it while it puts the words in at most one part more than beside the even box; past that the slide holds too much for one screen
boxes._need: the picture's share of the slide's width by the names it shows at once (a kit drawing's labelled parts, a 3D scene's labels, an SVG's words, a photograph's spots): up to 6 any box, 7-10 even, 11-15 picture-wide, 16-22 picture-large, 23 or more the whole slide. Starting values; a drawing whose words the audit finds too small or crowded is given the next box by the layout solver
boxes._three_d: a 3D model beside words always has at least picture-wide (2.69.0: at 40-50 % the models were almost invisible)
boxes._wide_aspect: a picture this many times wider than high is drawn small in a box beside words: across the slide (figure-stage) when the words allow it
boxes._top_row_aspect: the row's photographs together at most this many times as wide as high (two 16:9, three 3:2): more of them in one row are drawn too low to read (M01 s03: four ships of 2:1, 70 px high) - they stay beside the words, two a row
boxes._top_aspect: photographs this many times wider than high (every tile, or the one photograph in its own column) are shown in a row on top, each box the photograph's own shape, the words under them (the variant figure-top of explain-figure, reading-with-figure and content-in-parts) while the words fit under_top_row; in a tall box beside the words a wide photograph is drawn small between two empty bands (M01 s09). A tall or square photograph stays beside the words

variety._why: owner, 2026-10-21 (L62): 'make sure that two types of slides never repeat in a row - now 6-7 slides are exactly the same layout, and it hurts the eyes'. 2.118.0 made a repeat a note; the owner, 2026-11-11, asks for variety again - the deck's shapes are planned over the whole module ("shapes" below, compile/scripts/layout_plan.py), on in every build. The old way of flipping one slide at a time (the picture on the other side, the other ground) runs only in the factory's own tests, CF_LAYOUT_FLIP=1.
variety._measured: 2.63.0: framed photo 100 -> 50 and picture-top 110 -> 70 words, from the measured budgets below (IGF M04 s05: 102 words under a photograph across the slide spilled 66 px)
variety._stop_at: the run of slides that look the same the layout flip acts on (factory tests only). A slide the script marks as a comparison (the compare-two or before-after template, a comparison picture, a title that compares or says before / after) may take the look of the slide before it on purpose
variety._shape: the shapes the eye sees are "shapes" below; the old flip (factory tests only) still names picture-right, picture-left, picture-top, photo-full, photo-framed and text

shapes._why: owner, 2026-11-11, after a test build: 'all slides look same, only sides changes, but picture + text is almost same every slide, we need to change that ... put images up and text down, and images down and text up'. A slide's look is its SHAPE - where its picture sits against its words - never its template's name: a picture on the left and one on the right are one look (beside). Each blueprint (knowledge/blueprints/<template>.<variant>.json) names its shape - the one place: the compiler's plan (compile/scripts/layout_plan.py), the package check (check_course_package.py) and the trial's scorecard (factory_trial.py) all read it there. A template with no shape ("") is not a teaching slide - a task launch or the recap - and breaks a run.

names.beside: the picture left or right of the words
names.top: a picture band across the slide, the words under it
names.bottom: the words first, a picture band across the slide under them
names.stage: the picture is the slide, a short caption
names.photo-full: a photograph across the whole slide, the words on it
names.words: words only - text, cards, key numbers, steps with no picture
names.two: two pictures - compare, before and after

shapes._band_templates: the templates whose words can sit under (figure-top) or over (figure-bottom) a picture band across the slide. A band holds a photograph, a row of them, a 2D-kit or kit drawing or a live 3D scene when the picture is wide (band_aspect); the words under or over it take two columns. three-content-blocks keeps its blocks beside the one scene whose parts they name. The templates that have the room answer (scenario, worked-example, true-false, name-parts) keep their picture beside the words while its box takes the picture, and take their own band (figure-top, figure-bottom: the picture across the slide, their columns under or over it) when the picture is too wide for it - never the tall box beside the words
shapes._band_aspect: a picture this many times wider than high goes in a band: a photograph by its pixels (as the row on top, boxes top_aspect), a 2D-kit or kit drawing by its size or viewBox, a 3D scene by its home view's bounding box seen from the spec's view (az, el). A long ship profile, a hull section, a pipeline or a deck plan are wide; a tall tank, a person, a mast are not - they keep their height beside the words
shapes._band_names: the most names a picture in a band shows at once (a kit drawing's labelled parts, a 3D scene's labels; boxes need: 11-15 is picture-wide) - the band gives them the slide's width but less height; more go beside the words in the box they need, or on the stage
shapes._plan: the compiler plans every deck's shapes before it builds a slide: for each teaching slide the shapes it fits (its words within that shape's budget, its picture's natural shape, the names it shows), then the choice that never puts the same shape twice in a row, keeps beside to at most beside_share of the teaching slides and, in a module of min_slides teaching slides or more, uses at least min_shapes shapes - changing as few slides as it can, prefer the order it tries another shape in. A slide whose build sheet names a template, a variant or a layout ("composition") keeps it; so does a slide that fits only one shape (a note names it and why). A comparison may take the shape of the slide before it (variety _stop_at). The planner never cuts or moves a word: it only picks among the shapes the slide already fits. The same input gives the same plan. A shape the build's audit measured out (MNN_layout_avoid.json) is not planned again while the slide's words are the same

dense._why: 2.116.0: a NOTE only - 'dense' is more than 60 words on the slide. A dense slide may have no picture when its words read on their own; there is no picture quota. The factory never cuts or moves words. How many words a slide carries is the one word guideline in course-factory/knowledge/theory-rules.json "slide".

parts._why: 2.116.0 (operator, 2026-11-09): the factory NEVER pages the words by itself. auto_from_words is only the writer's threshold (v_paged_slide: more words than a picture's column holds - the writer shortens them with the operator's approval); content-in-parts is built only when a build sheet asks for it ("template": "content-in-parts" / "parts"), then its lines in order, in parts of about part_words words, Next walks the parts. A slide with no picture and more than the word guideline's steps_from (course-factory/knowledge/theory-rules.json "slide") is shown in parts the same way, beside nothing. 2.63.0: 135 / 110 were starting values; measured (see budgets) the column beside a picture holds 85 words at 1024 x 768 and a part 75 - 90-135 words beside a picture spilled 19-91 px, a part of 85 spilled 68 px.

budgets._why: 2.63.0 - how many words fit, MEASURED with the real compiler, these templates and the larger logo: four texts of every length cut from the IGF Basic scripts' own lines (a statement and bullets), each slide alone between short text slides, judged by run_audits.py (the build's gate) at 1024 x 768 - the binding size - and 1280 x 800. A budget is the longest length at which all four fitted. The compiler's layout choice uses them (the thresholds above and below are set from them), and a slide built over its layout's budget gets an early warning at compile.
budgets._table: a table slide (reference-table: the lines with cells separated by " | ") is measured by its rows and its words - both must fit, the words alone do not say it: a row is a line of the table however few words it holds. Measured with measure_word_budgets.py at 1024 x 768, 1280 x 800 and 1280 x 720, a table of 2 columns, the first cell two words, rows 3-8 and 5-14 words a row, on the first factory trial's lines: beside a picture (table_beside; a drawing or a photograph, the same) and alone (table_alone) every table of up to 6 rows and 48 words fits (6 rows of 11 words spilled 29-84 px at 1024 x 768, 8 rows of 8 words 39-142 px, 5 rows of 14 words 24-56 px); across the slide under or over a picture band (table_under_band, table_over_band, table_under_top_row, table_over_photo_row - the same for a drawing, a 3D scene, photographs or tiles) the band keeps its least height, so up to 4 rows and 40 words fit (4 rows of 14 words spilled; 5 rows of 6 words spilled 19-31 px, 6 rows 77-84 px). A table over the budget of every shape its picture can take is a must-fix at the script (t_table_over): split the table or use two slides - the text is never made smaller. M01 s03 (6 rows, 73 words) and s14 (6 rows, 57 words) were cut 66 and 21 px at 1024 x 768 beside a picture before
budgets._under_top_row: a picture band across the slide, the words under it (figure-top) or over it (figure-bottom): measured 2026-11-11 with measure_word_budgets.py at 1024 x 768, 1280 x 800 and 1280 x 720 on the first factory trial's scripts - a row of two 3:2 photographs (under-top-tiles, over-bottom-tiles), one photograph (over-bottom-photo) and a 2.5:1 kit drawing (under-band-drawing, over-band-drawing), the band never lower than 30 vmin (240 px at 1280 x 800) as its grid row's least height: every text fits up to 70 words, at 80 one spills 20-51 px at 1024 x 768; a part of two in a band (parts-under-band-drawing, parts-under-top-tiles) up to 40 (part_band; 50 spilled 11-40 px). The 100 measured before for the row on top was a box taller than its row lying over the words - the audits did not see it; the band's least height is now its row's, and a slide too full scrolls. Beside a tall picture (beside-tall-photo, a 3:4 photograph, the words 62 %) every text fits up to 50 (beside_tall; 55 spilled 10 px)
budgets._worked_column: a worked example's steps are cards, so the words are not all that fills its column: each line is a card (its padding, card px, and its rows of row px, about row_words words a row), gap px between them, a subheading (a short line ending with ":") head px. Measured at 1024 x 768 on the first factory trial's nine worked examples (M01 s05: six lines, 61 words, a column of 504 px where the slide body has 472 under a two-line title; the sum came within 25 px of every measured column). Over px the steps do not fit beside the picture: content_script.py t_overfull_rows, a must-fix like t_overfull
budgets._worked_under: a worked example's question and, on its last Next, its answer are cards under the picture, in the picture's column (compile_module.answer_over): the picture keeps what they leave. Measured at 1024 x 768 on the first factory trial's four worked examples (M01 s02, s13, M19 s11, s12; M01 s02: a 3D scene, a 14-word question, a 3-line 46-word answer, the scene left 171-194 px and its labels cut at the top): the column is 521 px under a one-line title (up to title_chars characters), 472 under a two-line one; the question card 51 px and 25 px a row of about 8 words, the answer card 32 px and 20 px a row of about 8 words, 12 px between the cards and the picture - the sum came within 30 px of the four measured pictures (171-229 px). The picture keeps at least 240 px (30 vmin, as the row of photographs on top), so the two cards and their gaps take at most px (px_long_title under a two-line title). Over it: content_script.py t_overfull_under, a must-fix like t_overfull
budgets._remeasured: 2026-11-12, after the tappable lines got their 44 px (gb_compose.css): every layout of measure_word_budgets.py at its budget at 1024 x 768, 1280 x 800 and 1280 x 720 on the first factory trial's lines. Over: photo_column 85 (spilled 10-49 px at 1024 x 768; now 75), beside_picture_with_inset 70 (27 px; now 65), under_top_photo 70 (31-157 px; now 60), and the bands under_top_row, over_photo_row, under_band, over_band 70 (one text 20 px at 1024 x 768; now 65). Held: beside_picture 85, part 75, part_band 40, beside_tall 50, photo_full 50, photo_framed 50 (the 17-28 px measured there at any word count was the photograph's own slow zoom, not words - no longer counted), every table budget, and the four bands of the templates that have the room answer. Not measured by the tool: beside_3d, stage, scenario_situation, scenario_choices, worked_steps (the fit gate measures those slides at build)
budgets._band_active: the band of a template that has the room answer (figure-top, figure-bottom: a picture too wide for the box beside its words, the template's columns under or over it). Measured 2026-11-12 with measure_word_budgets.py (its ACTIVE layouts, walked by fit_gate.py at every Next) at 1024 x 768, 1280 x 800 and 1280 x 720 on the first factory trial's lines, a 2.5:1 photograph in the band, the band's least height 24 vmin: a scenario's situation up to 40 (scenario_situation_band; 50 spilled), its question, choices and whys, side by side under the situation, up to 70 (scenario_choices_band; under the band 80 fitted, over it 80 spilled); a worked example's steps with its question as t_part_steps counts them up to 40 (worked_steps_band: 30 words of steps under a 10-word question fitted, 35 spilled over the band, 40 under it); a true or false's why up to 30 (true_false_band; 40 spilled). Over its band's budget a slide is split in two (content_script.py t_part_*, t_no_shape), never made smaller
budgets._active: a scenario beside a picture: its situation under the picture (scenario_situation), its question, choices and whys in the other column (scenario_choices); a worked example (and any slide with a question and its answer) beside a picture: its lines and the question (worked_steps), the question and on the last Next its answer under the picture. Measured by the fit gate on the first factory trial's four modules at 1024 x 768. These templates have no parts and no larger box, so content_script.py makes a script over them a must-fix at render (t_overfull), naming the budget and the split - two slides, the second may carry its own picture; the fit gate stays the final stop at build.
budgets._first_spill: beside a picture 90 words (2 of 4 texts, 19 px), with a photo under the words 75 (1/4, 10 px), photo column 90 (2/4), under a top photo 75 (3/4, 71 px; one 55-word text spilled 31 px), on a full-screen photo 55 (1/4), framed photo 60 (2/4, 40 px), two parts of 85 words (3/4, 68 px)

long_title._why: every budget was measured under a one-line title. At 1024 x 768 a title wraps to two lines past chars characters (measured on the gas trial's M01 deck: titles of up to 35 characters stood on one line, of 36 and more on two - the title 49 px, then 97), and the slide body loses px of its body px. Beside a picture, and on the stage, the budgets held under a two-line title (M01 s04: 59 words beside a 3D scene; s14: 66; s01: 41 under a picture that is the slide). Under or over a picture across the slide (band_budgets) they did not: the band keeps its least height (30 vmin, 230 px at 1024 x 768, and the gap - band px), so the whole line comes off the words - M01 s11 (59 words under a 16:9 photograph, a 43-character title) was cut 29 px and s20 (64 words under a 3D scene, 42 characters) 65 px at 1024 x 768, the layout plan having counted the words alone. Under a two-line title a band budget is its words (and a table's rows) times (body - band - px) / (body - band): 65 becomes 53. The layout plan, the script check and the fault report count it (compile/scripts/layout_plan.py holds, options); a slide no shape then holds is split, or its title made shorter - the words are never made smaller

explain-figure.name: Text + figure
explain-figure.auto: a split or column layout with a picture, up to 60 words; text-only: a short slide with no picture

figure-stage.name: Large figure
figure-stage.auto: layout visual_full or visual_wide with a drawing and few words

photo-explain.name: Photo + explanation
photo-explain.auto: a photograph: full screen, beside the words, or in its own column

compare-two.name: Comparison
compare-two.auto: a build sheet with "figure_b" and "blocks" of two line ranges (2.127.0 - "template" is not needed)

procedure.name: Sequence of actions
procedure.auto: a slide whose lines are numbered steps

task-launch.name: Task opening
task-launch.needs: a task slide or a room activity
task-launch.auto: every task slide and room activity

recap.name: Summary
recap.auto: the recap slide - one design for every module (L51)

long-explanation.name: Long explanation + 3D
long-explanation.needs: a 3D figure and more than 60 words; points: the script's "points"
long-explanation.auto: a 3D slide with dense text; points: a slide with "points" - the short points beside the picture, the full words in the instructor's notes

three-content-blocks.name: Three content blocks
three-content-blocks.auto: a build sheet with "blocks" of three line ranges (2.127.0 - "template" is not needed)

reference-table.name: Table + conclusion
reference-table.needs: figure + lines with cells separated by " | "
reference-table.auto: a slide whose lines are table rows

reading-with-figure.name: A lot of text + figure
reading-with-figure.auto: a split or column layout with a picture and dense text

content-in-parts.name: One slide, several parts
content-in-parts.needs: figure; "parts": line ranges, or more than 85 words
content-in-parts.auto: a slide with a picture and more than 85 words (parts.auto_from_words)

worked-example.name: Worked example, then your turn
worked-example.needs: "active": "worked-example", the steps as lines ("what you do | what you get"), "ask" and "reveal"
worked-example.auto: a worked example with the room's turn

name-parts.name: Name the parts
name-parts.needs: a static 3D render or a photograph, "ask", the names as lines, the build sheet's "spots" for every line

key-numbers.name: Numbers to remember
key-numbers.needs: 3-8 lines "value | what it means", no picture
key-numbers.auto: lines that are numbers and their meaning

before-after.name: Spot the difference
before-after.needs: two pictures ("figure", "figure_b"); the first line names the two states "A | B", each line after it "what | in A | in B"
before-after.auto: two pictures and lines in that shape

drill.name: Quick drill
drill.needs: "drill"; quick-fire: lines "prompt | answer"; say-it: the situation as lines, "ask", "reveal"; find-it: a photograph and "spots"
drill.auto: a slide with "drill", just before the module check

picking._why: The templates hold no words of their own; the factory picks the right one for each piece of a new course's information. It reads what each piece of the module's information is and writes the script so (content script fields) and the build sheet so (pictures); the compiler then builds the template. Read by the script guide (script/GUIDE.md section 5c) and the compiler (shaped_template, auto_template). Always: never the same look twice in a row (L62), each picture by the picture rule (L67, course-visuals SKILL.md).

rows.info: a picture and a short explanation
rows.how: the lines beside a 3D model or a photograph
lines "1 ...", "2 ..." - step boxes when there is no picture
build sheet "template" and "blocks": three line ranges, one 3D scene
"points": 3-5 short points on the slide; "text" keeps the full words for the instructor
"active": "worked-example", the steps as lines, "ask" the room's turn, "reveal" its answer
"claim" the belief, "claim_is" false (or true), the lines why

rows.info: what to do when something happens

rows.how: "ask", the part names as lines; the build sheet's "spots" on a static 3D render or a photograph
lines "value | what it means", no picture

rows.info: two states of the same thing
rows.how: lines "A | B" then "what | in A | in B"; build sheet "figure" and "figure_b"
"recap": true, and "asks": one question for each line
"before" on the task slide that opens it: 2-4 things to check

rows.info: before the module check, every second or third module
rows.how: "drill": quick-fire, say-it or find-it, after the module's last teaching slide

mix._why: 2.127.0 (operator Aleksis Vejs, 2026-11-10: 'the factory doesn't really want to use the template'). Counted on the built decks: Project Management 42 of 57 teaching slides plain (a picture beside ordinary lines), the safety course 150 of 150; ten of the twenty-one templates in no deck at all. The picking table was an invitation only - nothing said when a slide's own words already had the shape of a template. Now the script check (content_script.template_findings) reads every PLAIN teaching slide - no field or line shape of a template, no template asked for in the build sheet - and names the template its words fit and how to write them (t_fits_template, a suggestion). The module is a MUST-FIX (t_template_mix) only when more than max_plain_share of its teaching slides are plain AND the check can name slides that fit a template: there is always something concrete to do, and no rule to satisfy by guessing. The operator who wants the module plain says why ("plain_why" at the top of the script): then a note.
mix._values: starting values - 0.6: the two courses counted above are over it, a module with four plain slides in ten is not. min_slides: a module too short to judge is left alone.
mix._label_words: a line 'Label: text' or 'Label - text' is a named part when its label is this many words or fewer

signs._why: words that say what a piece of information is, by course language. Only English is listed; a course in another language gets the checks that read the lines' shape (headings, labels, numbers, a calculation, a question), which need no words.
